newsitem.title: GERMANY: Airbus must become more competitive - Dasa.
newsitem.headline: Airbus must become more competitive - Dasa.

text.p: European aeropace consortium Airbus Industrie must turn into a streamlined, integrated company with a broader product line to meet the challenges of the Boeing Co -McDonnell Douglas Corp merger, the group's German member said in a radio interview.

Airbus must give up its present structure as a partnership and quickly build up a competitive organization integrating design, engineering and manufacturing, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) chief Manfred Bischoff told Bavarian Radio on Sunday night.
The group would need two years to make such a change, he said.
Airbus must also add new products, such as wide-body planes for more than 500 passengers, a highly profitable segment dominated by Boeing Co, Bischoff said.
"To do that, it means getting technological advances like our American competitors get them," Bischoff said.
Bischoff added that Airbus, like its competitor, should have no special state role.
The merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas Corp, if approved by U.S. regulators, would create the world's largest aerospace company with annual sales of $48 billion and more than 200,000 employees.
Dasa, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, is pushing its vision of Airbus against those of its partners.
France's Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, which like Dasa owns 37.9 percent of Airbus, favours a minimal organisation that would manage the work of subcontractors.
British Aerospace Plc, a 20 percent owner, prefers retaining "core assets" such as production and design facilities.
Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa) owns four percent of Airbus.
